split_reasoning: Patrolling and checking access points are parts of the same physical security round.

parts.text: Patrol premises and check doors, windows, and gates for intrusion or security weaknesses.
parts.type_reasoning: The guard moves around the premises and physically checks access points.

split_reasoning: Responding to an alarm and investigating the disturbance are stages of the same on-site response.

parts.text: Respond to an alarm and investigate the disturbance at the location.
parts.type_reasoning: Investigating ordinarily requires attending and checking the affected location.

notes: A separate written incident report is covered by task 2134.

split_reasoning: Checking and authorizing people at an entrance is a live interaction, while observing traffic for suspicious activity can also occur without an individual waiting for service.

parts.text: Check and authorize an employee, visitor, or other person's entrance or departure.
parts.type_reasoning: The person is present while the guard checks and grants or denies access.
parts.unit_reasoning: One person's access check is completed and communicated during the encounter.
parts.work_item: one entrance or departure checked and authorized or denied
parts.start: person presents themselves at the access point
parts.end: access decision is communicated and passage allowed or denied
parts.checked_by: the person seeking passage and site security management

parts.text: Observe entrance and departure traffic and flag a suspicious or unauthorized movement.
parts.type_reasoning: Continuous observation produces identifiable security events that can be flagged for action.
parts.unit_reasoning: A particular suspicious movement is the actionable item arising from surveillance.
parts.work_item: one suspicious entrance or departure identified and flagged
parts.start: guard observes movement suggesting an access or theft concern
parts.end: concern is flagged for security action

notes: The split and shares depend on whether the site separates access checks from surveillance.

split_reasoning: Daily activity and irregularity reports are the same kind of written reporting work, with different content.

parts.text: Write a report of security activities or an irregularity observed on duty.
parts.type_reasoning: Each report is a distinct written record used by others.
parts.unit_reasoning: A completed shift or incident report is submitted and reviewed as a whole.
parts.work_item: one completed daily activity or incident report
parts.start: reporting period ends or an irregularity requires documentation
parts.end: completed report is submitted or entered into the reporting system
parts.checked_by: security supervisor, client, or incident investigator

notes: Report length and format vary between routine shifts and significant incidents.

split_reasoning: Calling police or fire services is one emergency notification activity with alternative recipients.

parts.text: Notify police or fire services of an emergency and request assistance.
parts.type_reasoning: The call produces a specific emergency notification and request that the dispatcher acts on.
parts.unit_reasoning: One emergency notification is relayed to the appropriate dispatch service as a whole.
parts.work_item: one emergency notification and request for response
parts.start: guard identifies an emergency requiring police or fire assistance
parts.end: dispatcher receives the location and relevant emergency details

notes: The guard is requesting emergency service rather than serving a waiting customer.

split_reasoning: Circulating among people to preserve order and protect property is one physical security activity.

parts.text: Circulate among visitors, patrons, or employees to preserve order and protect property.
parts.type_reasoning: The work requires the guard's physical presence and movement among people.

split_reasoning: Taking a message for someone else and answering an information question are different outputs of live calls.

parts.text: Take a caller's message when the switchboard is closed or during non-business hours.
parts.type_reasoning: The guard obtains the message from the caller during a live telephone contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: One message is taken for its intended recipient during the call.
parts.start: caller asks to leave a message
parts.end: message and contact details are taken and confirmed with the caller
parts.checked_by: the caller and the intended message recipient

parts.text: Answer a caller's question or provide requested information when the switchboard is closed or during non-business hours.
parts.type_reasoning: The answer is provided while the caller is on the telephone.
parts.unit_reasoning: A caller's information request is handled and answered within the contact.
parts.start: caller asks a question or requests information
parts.end: available information or an appropriate referral is given to the caller

notes: Shares vary with the site's call mix; message delivery after the call is not separately specified.

split_reasoning: Warning a person is a verbal interaction, whereas apprehending or evicting a violator requires physical intervention.

parts.text: Warn a person that they are violating premises rules.
parts.type_reasoning: The warning's value is in the live interaction with the person.

parts.text: Apprehend or evict a violator from the premises, using force when necessary.
parts.type_reasoning: Apprehension or removal requires physical presence and may require hands-on intervention.

notes: The shares depend on how often warnings escalate to apprehension or eviction.

split_reasoning: Operating screening equipment is one on-site screening activity, regardless of the detecting device used.

parts.text: Operate detecting devices to screen people for prohibited articles before entry.
parts.type_reasoning: Screening requires physical operation of equipment and handling of people or belongings at the checkpoint.

split_reasoning: Escorting on foot and driving are alternative physical means of accompanying and protecting a person.

parts.text: Escort or drive a person to a location or provide personal protection during movement.
parts.type_reasoning: The guard must physically accompany or drive the person.

split_reasoning: Inspection and adjustment are connected steps in checking security equipment for operation and tampering.

parts.text: Inspect and adjust security systems or equipment for operational readiness and signs of tampering.
parts.type_reasoning: The work requires on-site examination and physical adjustment of equipment.

split_reasoning: Building controls may be monitored and adjusted at a computer or physically at the equipment, which are different work settings.

parts.text: Monitor building-system controls on a computer and adjust a setting when needed.
parts.type_reasoning: Computer monitoring produces individual control adjustments that building staff rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: A response to a particular system condition is completed as one control adjustment.
parts.work_item: one building-system control adjustment made through a computer
parts.start: reading or alert indicates that a setting needs adjustment
parts.end: setting is changed and the resulting status is checked

parts.text: Check and adjust building-system controls at the equipment.
parts.type_reasoning: This work requires the guard to attend and physically operate local controls.

notes: The mix of computerized and local controls varies substantially by building.

split_reasoning: Locking doors and gates is one physical securing activity involving different access points.

parts.text: Lock entrance and exit doors and gates to secure buildings.
parts.type_reasoning: The guard physically attends and locks the access points.

split_reasoning: Administering first aid is hands-on care, while obtaining paramedic assistance is a separate request for emergency response.

parts.text: Administer basic first aid during a medical emergency.
parts.type_reasoning: First aid requires hands-on care at the person's location.

parts.text: Obtain paramedic assistance for a medical emergency.
parts.type_reasoning: The request communicates an emergency and its location to a dispatcher who arranges a response.
parts.unit_reasoning: One request for paramedic response is relayed for a particular emergency.
parts.start: guard identifies a medical emergency requiring paramedics
parts.end: dispatcher receives the location and relevant medical emergency details
